terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation; from what, ab or the ablative
evidence: Ov. Met. 14.266–267: sparsōsque sine ōrdine flōrēs sēcernunt calathīs
terms.comment: Sorting as separating: the good from the bad, one kind from another, each into its basket.

evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.1.23: dīligentissimē lēgī et dīgessī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Sorting as putting in order: papers, books, a library (Suet., Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: grāmina dispōnunt sparsōsque sine ōrdine flōrēs sēcernunt calathīs variāsque colōribus herbās
phrases.english: they lay out the plants, and sort into baskets the flowers strewn anyhow and the herbs of different colours

phrases.latin: lēctāsque crībrāre et sēcernere, quaecumque maculōsae, vitiōsae minōrisve incrēmentī vidēbuntur
phrases.english: and to sieve the picked olives and sort out any that look spotted, damaged or undersized

sources: Lewis & Short: secerno · Lewis & Short: digero

Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cato, which also holds Columella; loci-ovidius), checked against the editions named there; Ovid (Met. 14.266–267) checked against the Perseus Latin texts.
